summary.headline: Bare or nearly bare for 5.0 months a year (Dec-Apr); 23% of the year's erosive rain lands on that exposed soil.

why.text: This is what the field does today. Every alternative is measured against it with the same models, so the comparison is like for like.
Where it holds up: save water and ride out drought; income, forage and markets.
Where the data shows strain: break pest, weed and disease cycles; build organic matter and nitrogen.
Staying with it is a legitimate choice. It needs no new equipment, markets or learning, and its risks are ones you already know.

evidence.dataset: MERRA-2 meteorology + GPM IMERG precipitation (daily, point)
evidence.statement: About 2399 mm of rain a year
evidence.detail: Year-to-year swing is 13%. The wettest months are Sep, Oct, Nov. Annual total is rising 162 mm per decade (a clear trend).

evidence.dataset: Daily rain gauge: Penang International (MYM00048601)
evidence.statement: Satellite rain reads 5% higher than the nearest rain gauge
evidence.detail: Penang International gauge, 106 km away: 2390 mm; GPM IMERG 2503 mm; MERRA-2 2287 mm a year. The fused estimate leans 10% on the gauge, less the farther away it is.

evidence.dataset: MERRA-2 meteorology + GPM IMERG precipitation (daily, point)
evidence.statement: 46% of the year's soil-moving rain falls in Sep, Oct, Nov
evidence.detail: 56 days a year bring more than 12.7 mm. The biggest single day on record was 138 mm. Heaviest-day rainfall is rising 6.7 mm per decade (a clear trend).

evidence.dataset: MERRA-2 meteorology + GPM IMERG precipitation (daily, point)
evidence.statement: 2 days a year reach 35 C
evidence.detail: The last eight years averaged 2 such days against 1 in the first eight. The count is flat over the record. Mean temperature is rising 0.28 C per decade (a clear trend).

evidence.dataset: MERRA-2 meteorology + GPM IMERG precipitation (daily, point)
evidence.statement: No frost: the monsoons, not temperature, set the planting calendar
evidence.detail: The wettest three months are Sep-Nov (891 mm) and the driest Jan-Mar (290 mm). Rain exceeds evaporative demand in 10 months of the year, so a second or third crop depends on where the dry months fall and on irrigation.

evidence.dataset: MERRA-2 meteorology + GPM IMERG precipitation (daily, point)
evidence.statement: Rain exceeds evaporative demand 2.1 times over the year
evidence.detail: Reference evapotranspiration is 1168 mm a year against 2399 mm of rain. In Jan-Mar demand exceeds rain by 72 mm.

evidence.dataset: Root-zone soil wetness GWETROOT, standing in for SMAP L4
evidence.statement: 0.8 notably dry root-zone months a year recently, 3.5 in the early 2000s
evidence.detail: A dry month is one where root-zone wetness sits more than one standard deviation below normal for that month. Driest years: 2002, 2005, 2016. Main-season root-zone wetness is rising 0.011 units (0-1 scale) per decade (not statistically clear yet).

evidence.dataset: Sentinel-2 L2A NDVI (B08/B04), SCL cloud mask
evidence.statement: From orbit the field looks bare or dormant in 4 months of the year
evidence.detail: Sentinel-2 (10 m) greenness (NDVI) averages under 0.30 in Mar-May, Oct and peaks at 0.88 in Dec (2020-2024, 85 clear looks).

evidence.dataset: Soil properties 0-100 cm (texture, SOC, bulk density, pH, CEC, water retention)
evidence.statement: Acrisols (clay loam, SoilGrids 250 m), 7.8% organic matter
evidence.detail: The root zone can hold about 202 mm of plant-available water. pH 5.6, drainage: moderately well drained.

evidence.dataset: Soil properties 0-100 cm (texture, SOC, bulk density, pH, CEC, water retention)
evidence.statement: Hydrologic group C: this soil takes rain in slowly
evidence.detail: Erodibility (Kw) is 0.121, on a scale where 0.2 is resistant and 0.5 is very erodible. Tolerable loss is taken as 11 t/ha a year (a default; SoilGrids does not map soil depth to rock).

evidence.dataset: SRTM GL1 30 m elevation (3x3 window, Horn slope)
evidence.statement: Slope about 1.6% at 5 m elevation
evidence.detail: From SRTM 30 m elevation over a 180 m window (4 m of relief).

evidence.dataset: Crop cycles counted from Sentinel-2 NDVI peaks
evidence.statement: Sentinel-2 sees about 1.8 crop cycles a year
evidence.detail: Green peaks per year, 2020: 1, 2021: 2, 2022: 2, 2023: 3, 2024: 0. Crops usually peak in Jul, Nov. The satellite counts cycles; it does not name the crop.

evidence.dataset: Crop suitability index, high inputs (1981-2010 and 2041-2070 RCP8.5)
evidence.statement: FAO GAEZ rates this area's crop suitability
evidence.detail: Highest rated here: Hill rice (dryland padi bukit) (high, 76/100), Cassava (ubi kayu) (good, 62/100), Paddy rice (irrigated) (good, 61/100). Projected to lose most by the 2050s (RCP8.5): Sweet potato (-12 points).

evidence.dataset: Crop calendar from NASA POWER heat units and the monsoon rainfall pattern + RUSLE
evidence.statement: Bare or nearly bare for 5.0 months a year (Dec-Apr); 23% of the year's erosive rain lands on that exposed soil.
evidence.detail: Mean ground cover 54%; modelled soil loss 12.0 t/ha a year, 1.1 times the tolerable rate.

evidence.dataset: Monthly FAO-56 soil-water balance on fused rainfall and SoilGrids water-holding capacity
evidence.statement: Uses 939 mm of water a year; 20% of rain and irrigation goes through the crop
evidence.detail: Irrigation 408 mm a year (25% of the allocation). Runoff 191 mm, deep drainage 1474 mm, unmet crop demand 0%.

evidence.dataset: One-pool soil carbon balance driven by residue, roots, temperature and tillage
evidence.statement: Returns 5.5 t/ha of carbon a year; soil carbon trend -3.24 t/ha a year
evidence.detail: Living roots 8.0 months a year. Legume and cover-crop nitrogen credit 0 kg/ha a year.

evidence.dataset: 24 years of NASA POWER weather run through the rotation, every phase in every year
evidence.statement: Replaying 2001-2024 weather: RM2,784/ha on average, RM2,130 in a bad year
evidence.detail: Worst years: 2002, 2005, 2016. Weather alone moves net return by RM27/ha (one standard deviation).

benefits.summary: This is the reference. Benefits of the alternatives are measured against it.

items.topic: Rainfall (MERRA-2, bias-corrected): one pixel is 355x the width of this field
items.detail: Native resolution 55 km. Fused with IMERG and gauges by inverse-variance weighting.
items.close_by: A rain gauge or soil-moisture probe on the farm beats any pixel this size.

items.topic: Root-zone soil moisture (SMAP-class): a stand-in product was used
items.detail: SMAP L4 root-zone moisture (9 km) needs an Earthdata login. MERRA-2 wetness is the same kind of model-assimilated estimate at coarser resolution, so seasonal anomalies agree well but field-to-field differences are invisible.
items.close_by: Add a NASA Earthdata login to pull the native product, or check against a field sensor.

items.topic: Satellite check of the assumed crop calendar: weak agreement
items.detail: The crop calendar assumed for the current rotation and MODIS greenness move together (r = -0.19). The satellite does not see the calendar the tool assumed. The 250 m pixel may mix neighbouring fields, or the baseline rotation is wrong. Correct the baseline before trusting the comparison.
items.close_by: Edit the baseline rotation and planting dates to match your records.

items.topic: Compaction and hardpans below the surface
items.detail: No satellite sees a plough pan, and puddled paddy soils always have one. The model assumes roots can use the full soil depth; a compacted layer would cut water storage and the benefit of deep-rooted crops.
items.close_by: Push a penetrometer or dig a pit when the soil is moist, before switching a paddy field to dry-land crops.

items.topic: Soil life, nematodes and disease inoculum
items.detail: Nematode counts, disease carry-over and microbial activity are invisible from orbit. Pest scores use rotation rules of thumb, not what is in this soil.
items.close_by: Pull nematode and soil-health samples; review the field's disease history.

items.topic: Field drains, bunds, water gates and canals
items.detail: Drain spacing, bund height, the tertiary canal schedule and pump capacity are not in any public dataset. One on/off setting stands in for them.
items.close_by: Walk the drains and bunds; check the scheme's water-release schedule and raised-bed or drain options for dry-land crops.

items.topic: Varieties, hybrids and maturity groups
items.detail: Each crop is a single mid-range type (for paddy, a 105-115 day MARDI variety). Variety choice can move maturity by weeks and blast or drought tolerance by a lot.
items.close_by: Match variety duration and disease resistance to the planting windows shown, with the DOA or MARDI.

items.topic: Contracts, middlemen, rent and subsidies
items.detail: Prices are multi-year farm-gate averages. Contract farming terms, middleman margins, land rent, paddy input and price subsidies and Takaful cover can outweigh every number here.
items.close_by: Price each crop with your buyer, the PPK or FAMA, and check subsidy rules before committing land.

items.topic: Variation inside the field
items.detail: Weather inputs are 10-55 km pixels and the soil is a 250 m model estimate. Low spots that flood, sandy ridges and acid-sulphate patches are averaged away.
items.close_by: Walk the field after heavy rain and compare with the 10 m Sentinel-2 greenness; consider zoning the rotation.

gaps.statement: Scores are planning estimates from a monthly model. Treat a difference of fewer points than the uncertainty shown for that dimension as a tie, and treat every ringgit figure as a ranking aid, not a budget.

risks.title: Soil loss is above the tolerable rate
risks.detail: Modelled loss is 1.1 times what this soil can sustain. Staying the course means continued topsoil loss and silt in the rivers downstream.

risks.title: Paddy rice (irrigated) returns every 1 season(s)
risks.detail: Recommended gap is 2 seasons. Watch for brown planthopper, rice blast, weedy rice (padi angin) and for herbicide-resistant weeds selected by repeating the same programme.

risks.title: Soil is bare 5 months a year
risks.detail: Bare months coincide with part of the monsoon's erosive rain. Keeping straw or residue on the surface instead of burning it changes this without changing crops.

risks.title: Known risks are still risks
risks.detail: The current rotation's familiarity hides its exposure to one or two markets and one or two pest complexes.

The 250 m pixel may mix neighbouring fields, or the baseline rotation is wrong. Correct the baseline before trusting the comparison.

summary.headline: The soil is covered in every month of the rotation.

why.text: You ranked "keep soil covered and in place" highly, and this rotation scores +49 points on it against today (Rain that soaks in up from 92% to 97%).
You ranked "build organic matter and nitrogen" highly, and this rotation scores +19 points on it against today (Organic matter after 10 years up from -1.6 % points to -0.77 % points).
The field is bare 5.0 months a year now, and 46% of erosive rain falls in Sep-Nov. Cover crops (Sesbania green manure) cut bare time to 0.0 months.
Sesbania green manure fix nitrogen from the air: purchased nitrogen drops from 235 to 155 kg/ha a year.
No-till leaves residue on the surface: soil loss changes from 12.0 to 0.8 t/ha a year.

items.label: Irrigation pumped
items.meaning: Water applied per year, averaged over the rotation.

items.label: Total crop water use
items.meaning: Evaporation plus transpiration from the field.

items.label: Crop water stress
items.meaning: Share of crop water demand the soil and irrigation could not meet.

items.label: Organic matter after 10 years
items.meaning: Projected change in topsoil organic matter.

items.label: Purchased nitrogen
items.meaning: Fertiliser nitrogen needed after legume and cover-crop credits.

items.label: Nitrogen lost below roots
items.meaning: Residual nitrate carried down by drainage.

items.label: Rain that soaks in
items.meaning: Share of rainfall that enters the soil instead of running off.

items.label: Months with living roots
items.meaning: Months something is growing and feeding soil life.

items.label: Pest and disease break
items.meaning: Years between host crops, plant-family and planting-season diversity.

items.label: Net return
items.meaning: Revenue minus operating, labour, nitrogen, irrigation and cover-crop costs. Land rent and subsidies excluded.

items.label: Net return in a bad year (1 in 5)
items.meaning: Mean minus the swing from 2001-2024 weather replayed through the rotation and from price volatility.

items.label: Income swing (share of revenue)
items.meaning: Year-to-year standard deviation of net return divided by gross revenue. Lower is steadier.

risks.title: Cover-crop termination timing
risks.detail: A woody cover terminated late can tie up nitrogen and harbour pests. Agree a termination date and method (slash and mulch, roll, or incorporate two to three weeks before planting).

risks.title: Sesbania green manure ahead of paddy
risks.detail: Incorporate it 2-3 weeks before transplanting or broadcasting so it decomposes before the crop needs nitrogen.

risks.title: Paddy rice (irrigated) still returns sooner than recommended
risks.detail: Every 1 season(s) against a recommended 2. Scout for brown planthopper, rice blast, weedy rice (padi angin).

risks.title: Moving to no-till
risks.detail: Expect a 2-4 season transition: planting into residue, slug and rat pressure, and a different weed spectrum.

risks.title: Verify nitrogen credits before cutting fertiliser
risks.detail: Legume credits vary with stand, weather and termination date. Use a leaf-colour chart or in-season test the first seasons.

risks.title: Try it on part of the field first
risks.detail: A strip trial for two seasons tests the planting windows, equipment and markets with little at stake.

summary.statement: "Sweet corn + Paddy rice + Velvet bean → Sweet corn + Sweet potato + Velvet bean" fits your priorities best (74/100).

disclaimer: Kebunda surfaces patterns and possibilities from public data. It supports, and never replaces, the judgment of the farmer and of local agronomists, DOA and MARDI extension officers and crop advisers.
